text:
Evidence supports testing the objective before increasing attention capacity. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024 extended abstract; original RecSys 2023)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) attributes SASRec weaknesses to overconfidence under sampled BCE; replaces single-negative BCE with calibrated gBCE and multiple negatives, recommending calibration t=0.75 and 128–256 negatives. [Sampled-softmax analysis (2024)](https://zlstwebsite.github.io/Zlst/publication/on-the-effectiveness-of-sampled-softmax-loss-for-item-recommendation/) identifies implicit hard-negative weighting and connections to top-K ranking, although its experiments do not establish gains for this sequential Amazon benchmark. [Correcting LogQ (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that standard sampling correction mishandles the always-included positive; particularly relevant when using popularity-distributed in-batch negatives. Sampling-bias correction is distinct from correcting false-negative labels.

Harder negatives are not automatically better. [Adaptive Hardness Negative Sampling (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709) adjusts hardness during training to mitigate false-positive and false-negative problems; evidence concerns collaborative filtering, so transfer to SASRec remains a hypothesis. Suggested controlled comparison: retain the backbone and compare single-negative BCE, multi-negative BCE, gBCE, and sampled softmax at matched GPU budgets; then test a uniform/hard-negative mixture with gradual hardness increases. Exclude known training positives and duplicate target IDs from negative pools; unobserved relevance remains uncertain. Tune temperature and negative count using the pinned macro validation HR@10 across all four categories, inspecting Electronics separately. These sources establish plausible mechanisms, not improvement on this benchmark; training margins alone cannot select the winner.
